profile.name: JoAnna Mendoza
profile.bio: JoAnna Mendoza is a retired U.S. Marine with 20 years of service, including training military leaders. She has worked in public service and on veterans' transition issues, and describes herself as a rural Arizonan. She is the Democratic nominee for Arizona's 6th district.

platform.point: Wants to bring good-paying jobs to Southern Arizona and protect workers.
Focuses on lowering costs for families and seniors.
Pledges to strengthen the health care system.
Pairs safe communities and strong borders with immigration solutions.
Prioritizes climate, water and energy security for rural Arizona.
Commits to keeping promises made to veterans.

immigration.evidence: Platform combines strong borders with real immigration solutions.

foreign.evidence: Platform includes standing with U.S. allies.

profile.notes: Her issues page lists topic headings; detailed policy text was not captured.

profile.name: Daniel Butierez
profile.bio: Daniel Butierez is a third-generation Arizonan who runs two businesses, including a painting contracting company. He was the Republican nominee for Arizona's 7th district in 2024 and in the 2025 special election.

platform.point: Secure the southern border and give the U.S. Border Patrol the resources it needs.
Cut taxes and simplify the tax code for small businesses, moving toward a flatter system without the IRS.
Promote job growth in southern Arizona through responsible mining.
Address homelessness with an approach he describes as combining compassion and accountability.

economy.evidence: Calls for cutting taxes, a flatter tax code and eliminating the IRS.

immigration.evidence: Prioritizes securing the southern border and expanding Border Patrol resources.

profile.notes: His campaign policy page gives only short summaries, so most domains remain unscored.

profile.name: Peter Verbica
profile.bio: Peter Coe Verbica is a Republican candidate for California's 19th congressional district. He holds a law degree and is a certified financial planner. His campaign centers on lowering the cost of living in California.

platform.point: Wants to end high gas taxes and special fuel blend requirements.
Seeks more water for farmers to bring down food prices.
Pledges to address California's home insurance crisis.
Supports local control over housing decisions.
Opposes PAGA lawsuits and rules restricting independent contractors.
Calls for immigration reform that serves the technology and farm sectors.

economy.evidence: Opposes PAGA litigation and independent-contractor rules and wants lower taxes.

energy.evidence: Wants to end gas taxes and reformulated fuel blend requirements.

profile.notes: The campaign site lists his name as Peter Coe Verbica.

profile.name: Robin Littau
profile.bio: Robin Littau is the Republican nominee for California's 2nd Congressional District in 2026. Little public biographical information is available.
profile.notes: No campaign site, platform or voting record was found.

profile.name: Sandra Van Scotter
profile.current_role: Health care worker and disability advocate
profile.bio: Sandra Van Scotter is a Democratic candidate for California's 20th congressional district. She has about 20 years of experience in health care and has served on a local advisory committee for the Kern Regional Center's Self-Determination Program.

platform.point: Supports Medicare for All and a constitutional amendment making health care a right.
Opposes proposed cuts to Medi-Cal.
Pledges to advance access and inclusion for people with disabilities.
Promises town halls and direct office access for veterans and military families.
Backs border security plus legal status for long-settled undocumented workers.
Supports sustainable water policy for farmers and residents.

welfare.evidence: Supports Medicare for All as a constitutional right.

immigration.evidence: Supports a Reagan-style pathway to legal status for undocumented workers.

profile.name: Tessa Lynn Hodge
profile.bio: Tessa Lynn Hodge is a licensed clinical social worker who grew up in the High Desert region of California's 23rd District. She has worked with children in foster care and students needing school mental health services, and she helped San Bernardino County put state and federal legislation into county policy. This is her first campaign for Congress.

platform.point: Make health care more affordable and accessible.
Lower costs for homeowners and renters.
Bring good jobs with livable wages to the district.
Pursue a humane immigration policy.
Expand mental health resources and support.
Invest in public education.

immigration.evidence: Lists a humane immigration policy among her campaign priorities.

education.evidence: Lists investment in public education among her campaign priorities.

profile.notes: Campaign issues page names priorities without detailed policy proposals; Ballotpedia could not be reached.

profile.name: Joe Males
profile.bio: Joe Males is a member of the Hemet City Council and a small-business owner who started his own computer networking business in 1996. He is a Marine Corps veteran who served overseas and left the service as a sergeant. He ran for city council to focus on public safety after the murder of his son, also a Marine, which he discusses in his campaign biography.

platform.point: Make public safety and the rule of law a priority.
Improve infrastructure and support business growth in the Inland Empire and Imperial County.
Support veterans, drawing on his roles with veterans' organizations.

security.evidence: Centers his campaign on public safety and the rule of law.

profile.notes: No detailed policy platform was found on the campaign site.

profile.name: Jacqui Irwin
profile.bio: Jacqui Irwin has served in the California State Assembly since 2014, representing the 44th District and since 2022 the 42nd, and chairs the Revenue and Taxation Committee. She previously served as mayor and city council member in Thousand Oaks and worked as a systems engineer at Johns Hopkins University and Teledyne. Raised in Woodland Hills, she holds a systems engineering degree from UC San Diego.

platform.point: Address the rising cost of living, including federal action to ease construction barriers and fund affordable housing.
Oppose what she describes as Trump's attacks on democracy and shared values.
Expand gun safety measures, building on her gun violence restraining order legislation.
Cites her work reauthorizing California's climate law.
Improve wildfire resilience and access to home insurance.
Protect access to health care.

liberty.evidence: Authored legislation extending gun violence restraining orders to up to five years and campaigns on expanding gun safety (guns only).

energy.evidence: Highlights her role in reauthorizing California's climate law and authored recycled-plastic content requirements.

tech.evidence: Pushed AI companies to disclose training data and authored IoT device security requirements.

photo.author: Master Sgt. David J. Loeffler, California National Guard

profile.notes: Liberty score rests only on gun policy; no evidence found on her abortion, drug or speech positions, so it may shift once those are known.
